job.style: a passage rich in numbers, dates or measurements

passage: In the village of Rampur, the local governance structure is divided into three distinct levels. The foundation is the Gram Sabha, which includes every adult resident aged 18 or older who is registered on the electoral roll, not just the elected officials. This body meets to approve the annual budget and review the work of the Gram Panchayat. The Gram Panchayat itself consists of members elected by the villagers for a five-year term, led by a Sarpanch who must seek the approval of the ward members for major village decisions. Moving to urban areas, cities are divided into wards, and residents directly elect a Ward Councillor to represent their local needs in the Municipal Corporation. These councillors are not government appointees but are chosen by the people through local elections. At the district level, the Zila Parishad functions as the third tier of the Panchayati Raj system. It coordinates development activities across the district but does not possess the authority to create national laws, as that power belongs solely to the Parliament of India. By working together across these levels, the local government ensures that resources are managed effectively to improve the lives of all citizens in both rural and urban settings.

items.evidence: The foundation is the Gram Sabha, which includes every adult resident aged 18 or older who is registered on the electoral roll, not just the elected officials.
items.q: Meena, 19, is on Rampur's voter list but holds no post. What is her place in the Gram Sabha?
options: She is a member, like every adult voter
She is outside it, as only elected members belong
She is outside it, as only landowning men belong
She is a member only if the Sarpanch invites her
items.explain: Every registered adult aged 18 or older is in the Gram Sabha, not just elected officials.

wrong.why: thinks the Gram Sabha is only elected members
thinks only landowning men can attend

items.evidence: This body meets to approve the annual budget and review the work of the Gram Panchayat.
items.q: How do ordinary villagers in the Gram Sabha keep a say over the Gram Panchayat?
options: They pass its yearly budget and examine its work
They leave every decision to the Sarpanch alone
They fund it from their own pocket money
They send its problems to the Zila Parishad
items.explain: The Gram Sabha approves the annual budget and reviews the Gram Panchayat's work.

wrong.why: thinks the Sarpanch decides everything alone
thinks panchayat money comes from members' pockets
thinks the Zila Parishad handles single-village matters

items.evidence: The Gram Panchayat itself consists of members elected by the villagers for a five-year term, led by a Sarpanch who must seek the approval of the ward members for major village decisions.
items.q: Rampur's Sarpanch wants to build a new village school. What must happen first?
options: Get the ward members to agree to the plan
Get the district collector to agree to the plan
Get the Zila Parishad to pass a new law
Get money from the members' own pockets
items.explain: For major village decisions, the Sarpanch must seek approval of the ward members.

wrong.why: thinks the district collector controls the Sarpanch
thinks the Zila Parishad makes laws
thinks panchayat funds are members' pocket money

items.evidence: Moving to urban areas, cities are divided into wards, and residents directly elect a Ward Councillor to represent their local needs in the Municipal Corporation.
items.q: A broken streetlight troubles people in one city ward. Who should raise it in the Municipal Corporation?
options: The councillor they elected for their own ward
The councillor who looks after the whole city
The councillor the government appointed for the city
The councillor chosen by the Zila Parishad
items.explain: Residents of each ward directly elect a Ward Councillor to represent their local needs.

wrong.why: thinks a councillor covers the whole city
thinks councillors are appointed, not elected
mixes up rural and urban bodies

items.evidence: It coordinates development activities across the district but does not possess the authority to create national laws, as that power belongs solely to the Parliament of India.
items.q: A citizen wants a new law for all of India. Why can the Zila Parishad not make it?
options: Because only Parliament has that power
Because the Sarpanch must approve it first
Because the Gram Sabha must vote on it
Because it handles only one village's lanes
items.explain: The Zila Parishad coordinates district development; only Parliament can make national laws.

wrong.why: thinks the Sarpanch controls all decisions
thinks the village body ranks above the district
thinks the Zila Parishad looks after one village
